answer: An agent marketplace can require every new identity to earn a nontransferable reputation score through repeated, randomly assigned tasks, with peers staking deposits on each evaluation. A newcomer starts with little influence; trusted reviewers who approve fabricated work lose their stake when later audits expose it. Spinning up a hundred aliases therefore does not create a hundred trusted voices: the attacker must fund deposits and build histories over time. A sonnet about dawn and nectar might pass one task, but cannot cheaply manufacture that record.
